title: Partner can read the sharer's Locked Folder metadata when a search request omits visibility
summary:
### Summary

A partner can read the full metadata of every asset the sharer put in their Locked Folder. That
includes GPS coordinates, the on-disk path, the EXIF description and a thumbhash preview. The
partner gets it by calling the legacy search endpoints with the `visibility` field left out, while
their own session is unlocked with their own PIN.

The guard for this only fires when the client sends `visibility` explicitly. Leaving one optional
field out of the same request body gets past it.

| route | what the partner gets |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/search/metadata` | asset rows with `exifInfo` |
| `POST /api/search/statistics` | a count of the locked assets |
| `POST /api/search/random` | locked assets in the sample |
| `POST /api/search/large-assets` | locked assets listed |

Asset bytes stay protected. `GET /assets/{id}`, `/thumbnail` and `/original` are all refused, so this
is metadata rather than file access.

**How this differs from CVE-2026-108165.** That one is the partner sync stream:
`POST /api/sync/stream`, queried in `server/src/repositories/sync.repository.ts`. This is the search
path, queried in `server/src/utils/database.ts`. The two build their queries in different files and
share no code, so a fix to the sync queries will not change this behaviour. Both are present in
v3.3.3.

### Details

The legacy builder applies its visibility predicate conditionally:

```ts
// server/src/utils/database.ts:432-436
    .$if(!!options.visibility, (qb) =>
      options.visibility === 'not-locked'
        ? qb.where('asset.visibility', '!=', AssetVisibility.Locked)
        : qb.where('asset.visibility', '=', options.visibility!),
    )
```

`!!undefined` is `false`, so when `visibility` is omitted no visibility predicate is added at all.
The only ownership predicate in the builder is this:

```ts
// server/src/utils/database.ts:489
    .$if(!!options.userIds, (qb) => qb.where('asset.ownerId', '=', anyUuid(options.userIds!)))
```

and `userIds` still holds the partner ids, because the guard that strips them keys on the explicit
value:

```ts
// server/src/services/search.service.ts:356-360
  private async getUserIdsToSearch(auth: AuthDto, visibility?: AssetVisibility): Promise<string[]> {
    // Locked assets are personal. Never include partner IDs, regardless of A's elevated session.
    if (visibility === AssetVisibility.Locked) {
      return [auth.user.id];
    }
```

Five callers pass `undefined` as soon as the caller's own session is elevated
(`search.service.ts` lines 106, 128, 146, 161 and 193, each identical):

```ts
visibility: dto.visibility ?? (auth.session?.hasElevatedPermission ? undefined : 'not-locked'),
```

So for an elevated caller who omits the field there is no visibility filter, and
`ownerId IN (self, ...partners)`. Every partner's locked asset matches.

The V3 builder gets this right, which is where the fix should come from:

```ts
// server/src/utils/database.ts:814-816
      .where((eb) =>
        eb.or([eb('asset.visibility', '!=', AssetVisibility.Locked), eb('asset.ownerId', '=', scope.lockedOwnerId)]),
      )
```

That predicate is unconditional and scoped to the requester, so a locked row survives only if the
requester owns it. Sending `"filter": {}` routes to V3 and returns nothing, while the same query
without it leaks.

### Proof of concept

immich v3.3.1 in Docker. A is the victim, B the partner. A uploads an asset, sets a PIN, unlocks,
and sets the asset to `visibility: locked`. A shares with B. B turns it on in B's own timeline and
unlocks B's own session with B's own PIN. B never learns A's PIN, and holds no admin role, no API
key and no share link.

```http
POST /api/search/metadata
Authorization: Bearer <B, elevated session>

{"size":200,"withExif":true}
```

```json
{"assets":{"total":1,"items":[{
  "id":"fbf29e29-e631-486e-9b14-47c23fd31eb9",
  "ownerId":"b99e2116-db06-4613-9199-3cecb4...
